findings.observation: DOI 10.21037/jmai-2025-173 resolves correctly via Crossref to 'Deep learning precise image reconstruction algorithm for abdominal CT: impact on image quality and radiation dose reduction—a model validation study' by Xiaojing Liu et al., Journal of Medical Artificial Intelligence, published 2026-04 (online ahead 2025-07-28 per journal site article ID jmai-24-10776). findings.suggestedFix: No fix required for the DOI itself; keep 10.21037/jmai-2025-173. Optionally correct 'Liu Y et al.' to 'Liu X et al.' to match the actual first author (Xiaojing Liu) and add full author list (Liu, Ning, Liao, Gui, Wu, Lei) for precision.

findings.field: evidence[].doi — publisher internal article ID confusion
findings.observation: 'jmai-24-10776' is not a second DOI or an alternate/competing identifier for a different paper — it is AME Publishing's internal manuscript/article slug for the SAME article (URL https://jmai.amegroups.org/article/view/10776/html), assigned when the paper was received in 2024 (hence the '24' prefix) and later published with DOI suffix 'jmai-2025-173' reflecting the 2025 acceptance/publication-year numbering convention AME uses. It is not a registered Crossref DOI on its own (10.21037/jmai-24-10776 returns no Crossref record) and should not be treated as 'the real DOI' replacing jmai-2025-173.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep DOI as 10.21037/jmai-2025-173 (Crossref-registered, resolves, metadata matches). Do not substitute jmai-24-10776; it is only a publisher URL slug, not a citable DOI.

queries.query: openFDA 510(k) search applicant:Elekta sort by decision_date desc
openFDA 510(k) lookup K252188
FDA 510(k) database record K252188 (PMN lookup)
Innolitics FDA AI/ML device page for K252188 (CBCT reconstruction performance data)
Elekta press release — FDA 510(k) clearance for Elekta Evo linear accelerator

findings.observation: The actual 510(k) number IS now published: K252188, 'EMLA (Elekta Evo); EMLA (VersaHD); EMLA (Elekta Harmony Pro); EMLA (Elekta Infintiy); EMLA (Elekta Harmony); EMLA (Elekta Synergy)', applicant Elekta Solutions AB, decision date 2026-01-15 (Substantially Equivalent, product code IYE, regulation 21 CFR 892.5050, device class II). Innolitics' FDA AI/ML performance extract for K252188 explicitly lists an 'CBCT Image Reconstruction' algorithm ('Iterative reconstruction method using ordered subset and steepest descent') validated on 124 clinical datasets + 13 clinical patient CBCT projection datasets — this is the Iris reconstruction module bundled inside the whole-system EMLA linac clearance. The inventory's note 'K-number not yet published in FDA database as of Feb 2026' is now stale/incorrect, and the recorded decisionDate '2026-01-16' is off by one day versus FDA's official decision date of 2026-01-15 (2026-01-16 is the date of Elekta's press release announcing the clearance, not the FDA decision date).
findings.suggestedFix: Update regulatory.fda.clearanceNumber to 'K252188', decisionDate to '2026-01-15', and regulation/product code to 892.5050 / IYE (whole linac system clearance; Iris is a bundled CBCT reconstruction feature, not separately coded). Revise the notes field to remove the 'not yet published' language and instead state that Iris is cleared as the CBCT image-reconstruction feature within the EMLA (Elekta Evo/VersaHD/Harmony/Harmony Pro/Infinity/Synergy) 510(k), citing the Innolitics AI/ML performance table (124 clinical datasets, 13 patient CBCT projection datasets, iterative OS-SD algorithm).

findings.observation: Internal inconsistency: the top-level field evidenceRigor is set to 'E1', but the attached evidenceRigorNotes narrative concludes a Wave 5B investigation of three candidate iterative-CBCT publications by stating 'Neither vendor is named in the abstracts, so they cannot be attributed to IRIS Evo. E0 stands.' This reads as though the resolved/intended grade is E0 (vendor claims only, no attributable independent evidence), while the machine-readable evidenceRigor field was left at E1. The FDA AI/ML performance table for K252188 does show an internal validation on clinical data (124+13 datasets), which is sponsor-run V&V, not independent peer-reviewed evidence — consistent with an E0/E1 boundary call needing an explicit, unambiguous decision rather than a self-contradicting field+note pair.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction: either (a) set evidenceRigor to 'E0' to match the notes' explicit conclusion ('E0 stands'), since no independent peer-reviewed publication was attributable to IRIS Evo, or (b) if E1 is intentionally retained on the basis of the newly-identified FDA 510(k) sponsor V&V data (124 clinical + 13 patient CBCT datasets), rewrite evidenceRigorNotes to justify E1 explicitly rather than ending on an 'E0 stands' conclusion that contradicts the field value. Pick one and make field and narrative consistent.

findings.field: clinicalEvidence / limitations — FDA sponsor V&V dataset now available
findings.observation: Prior record states 'Validation evidence is currently limited to vendor brochures and press releases' and 'results': 'Not publicly disclosed'. The Innolitics AI/ML extract of K252188 now provides at least summary-level sponsor V&V detail (124 clinical image sets + 13 patient CBCT projection datasets, >1 reader) that was not reflected in the record.
findings.suggestedFix: Add this sponsor V&V detail to evaluationData.description/results, while still flagging it as non-independent, sponsor-run verification (not a peer-reviewed clinical study).
